prompt: Read-only technical review for a standalone experimental attractor explorer. The goal is coherent, clearly visible sculptural trajectories with continuous autonomous parameter evolution, absolutely no diffuse clouds/haze, no fake geometry or image crossfades, and no tanh. No scientific novelty claim is intended. Recommend concrete numerical methods and acceptance tests. Do not edit repository files or deploy anything.
context: Five finite-dimensional experimental modes: adaptive row-softmax 10-coordinate network with signed linear difference interactions and sine state update; Bayesian pairwise/quadratic learning with reversible probability pruning; discretized complex field with fractional memory, geometry and delayed nonlocal interactions; weighted ensemble using normalized products of group weights; single coupled system combining all layers.

Primary update U_next=(1-h)U+h*sin(a*U+b*(W*U-U)+c*F), with F_i=sum_j W_ij beta_ij (u_j-u_i). Features include energy, separation, covariance trace and spectrum, coherence, temporal variation, entropy and participation ratio. All closure choices are exploratory.

A previous parameter screening used fixed projections; strong chaos often gives point clouds and some candidate settings collapse to fixed points or simple cycles. Target: thin, irregular folded membranes, fine pale filaments, large negative-space cavities, asymmetric coherent structures on black. No rings-only defaults, no fabricated interpolation between unrelated point clouds. Rendering must be direct from computed data. Need mobile-friendly stable interaction and slow/fast evolution.
Current standalone browser source is not yet confirmed to be in this repository; please treat the above as the supplied design, do not claim to have inspected absent files.
expected_response: Prioritize 1) concrete shape metrics to reject clouds and collapse, distinguish coherent sheets from simple cycles; 2) parameter search and continuation algorithm to evolve through visible structures without artificial morphing; 3) how to avoid rendering artifacts; 4) meaningful slider sensitivity test protocol; 5) minimal pseudocode, failure cases and suggested defaults. Separate actual math changes from rendering. No code edits.
